cards.title: Hugging Face Launches Trainium Model Support Lookup Space for AWS Trainium Compatibility
cards.why_it_matters: If you ever evaluate or deploy models on AWS Trainium hardware, this space gives you instant compatibility data, shard counts, memory usage, and runnable scripts without trial-and-error compilation cycles.
cards.summary: A new Hugging Face Space surfaces a public dataset showing which Transformers models pass or fail on AWS Trainium2 (trn2) via torch-neuronx. Each entry records neuronx-cc compiler version, core count, wall time, peak memory, and a reproducible run.py. Currently covers text-generation and image-text-to-text models up to 16 Trainium2 cores; diffusers and other tasks are planned. A public NEFF cache lets users skip recompilation.

cards.title: LitPivot: AI System That Grounds Early Research Ideas in Literature, Beating Chat-Only Tools
cards.why_it_matters: As a research engineer who reads and produces papers, a system that automatically segments your proposal into problem/contribution/evaluation facets and critiques each against retrieved literature could meaningfully accelerate your own ideation and lit-review workflow.
cards.summary: LitPivot, built with UPenn collaborators and accepted to UIST 2026, splits a research proposal into problem, contribution, and evaluation facets, retrieves and groups related papers per facet, then generates literature-supported critiques with suggested revisions. In a 17-researcher study, domain experts rated LitPivot-developed ideas as better grounded; participants also perceived ideas as more novel and useful compared to a text editor plus AI chat baseline.
